speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have been experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the cause, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and how it feels?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the recent volleyball activity involving pivoting and twisting, are you experiencing pain specifically on the inner (medial) side of your knee, and does it worsen when you twist or squat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints). The location of pain over the medial tibia inferior to the patella, combined with recent increased physical activity and pivoting sports, is highly characteristic of this condition.
